findings.what: The asserted 28-versus-36 inventory-table revision difference is not real in the ROM data. InventoryCharsTable has 28 pointers in both revisions (REV02 0x0abc42..0x0abcb2, REV00 0x0abbd2..0x0abc42); InventoryNameStringTable has 27 in both (REV02 0x0abe2c..0x0abe98, REV00 0x0abdbc..0x0abe28). The next words are ASCII name data and the signed-byte auxiliary lookup, not additional pointers. Every corresponding pointer and its 14-byte target record translates by -112 bytes / remains identical. The corrected REV00 base addresses are correct, but the names-file prose and author report incorrectly interpret the former +32-byte mapping error as eight extra entries. Exact historical extern declaration spellings remain [INFERENCE].
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the corrected REV00 base addresses. Declare InventoryCharsTable[28] and InventoryNameStringTable[27] in both revisions, remove only the table-bound REVISION guard, and correct the extra-eight/36-entry provenance claims. The private recommended/inventory.c does this, still retaining the genuine DrawInventory idle-reset guard; all 37 functions MATCH both revisions and combined recommended full builds PASS. See revision-table-audit.json and the committed REV02 data_units.json 112-/108-byte pointer units.

findings.what: These new files declare ELEVATOR_POS_TABLE as a single char while change_level.c, level_changes.c, and the just-fixed region_walk.c/region_cleanup.c declare struct elevator_position[8]. Reads use the same leading bytes and match, but the declarations of the same cross-unit object are incompatible; the C008 table-type fix was not propagated into these new consumers.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse struct elevator_position { char x, y; } and the existing [8] declaration, accessing the first three pairs through .x/.y. Private recommended/transition_paths.c and recommended/map_population.c demonstrate all five functions MATCH both revisions; combined recommended ROM builds PASS.

findings.what: The same FontBackgroundByteMap is declared [28][40] in inventory and [32][40] in map drawing. The committed typed data unit is 1280 bytes / [32,40]; inventory merely consumes its first 28 rows. An extern declaration is not a separate leading-slice view.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the full [32][40] declaration in inventory while retaining the 28-row upload loop. Private recommended/inventory.c proves all 37 functions still MATCH both revisions and participates in both passing recommended full builds.

findings.what: The new func_01e38e declaration returns short, whereas its existing caller declares int. The packet returns a sign-extended word, which does not uniquely establish the original C return spelling; inventory ignores this result. No binary defect was observed, but the interface claims disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single evidenced return declaration. The minimal demonstrated choice is the existing extern int func_01e38e() in inventory; recommended/inventory.c matches both revisions. Alternatively choose short only with a checked migration of all callers. Do not present historical short-versus-int spelling as proved.

findings.what: Inventory newly declares gPlayerPoints as unsigned short[2], while main_loop.c declares short[]. Inventory has unsigned score comparisons; the existing main loop only increments the words. Bound completeness is compatible, but signed versus unsigned element types are not.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose a consistent score-word type. The private recommended/main_loop.c changes its declaration to unsigned short[] and MATCHes all 21 functions in both revisions; together with the recommended inventory file both full ROM builds PASS. This is a consistency proof, not a proof of the historical declaration.

findings.what: The new object_state and present_info definitions are offset-aligned with prior units but are not identical same-tag C types. Inventory splits reserved_30[27] into reserved_30[26]/value_4a and renames sprite to sprite_state; its present_info calls the second member identified where mole calls it reserved. The map units also add another map_player view of gPlayerInfo. Byte matching establishes the observed offsets/strides, not cross-unit C type compatibility. Several partial entity views already predate this checkpoint; this review does not claim they were introduced here.
findings.suggested_fix: Consolidate the shared entity/present declarations with the observed named fields, updating existing member accesses consistently, rather than continuing independent same-storage layouts. Preserve the observed offsets and 128-byte entity stride and check every affected unit in both revisions. No complete shared-layout consolidation was implemented or verified by this reviewer.

findings.what: C008Review F1-F4 were adopted, but its F5 scanner-comment correction was not. The comments still describe runs of four/five. Both scans reset the counter to one on a nonqualifying cell without clearing the remembered terrain label; one label, a gap, then three same-label qualifying cells can already trigger the interior threshold. The private scanner-counter-witness.json independently reproduces this source-level witness. Gameplay reachability and whether this was unintended remain [INFERENCE].
findings.suggested_fix: Describe counter thresholds and the preserved remembered-label/reset-to-one quirk, rather than claiming strictly contiguous runs. Keep executable code unchanged. If calling it an original bug, retain ORIGINAL BUG: and label the intent/reachability interpretation as [INFERENCE].

findings.what: The func_009934 comment calls the value written to both processed-input bytes B, but the code writes 64 (bit 6). The independently regenerated CheckAButton packet tests bit 6; ProcessInventory uses bit 4 to toggle the inventory and bit 6 for its present action. The adjacent func_0098f6 comment correctly calls the same 64 value the present-action button.
findings.suggested_fix: Say that the helper sets both input bytes to the present-action/A bit (0x40) before invoking CheckBButton, or simply name the bit without a button label. This is a comment-only correction.

qualification_summary: Both revisions reproduce exactly, including complete ROM builds, and the negative controls fail correctly. No blocking binary mismatch or prohibited matching device was observed. The medium qualification is the demonstrably false REV00 36-entry table claim; remaining findings concern cross-unit declaration consistency and comment accuracy. Any adoption of private recommended source changes requires a new immutable prepare/checkpoint.
